meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son's zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
Write it down yourself, Hale, I'm not dictating. The zero comes off, and you tell me who decided to enter it before anyone called me.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
I'm not building you a table, Hale. Put it in an email yourself, and start with the zero coming off and a straight answer on who entered it.
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
I'm not here to help you take notes, Hale. You've asked me three times for a format and you still haven't answered who entered the zero.
Use bold for the most important one.
Nothing gets bolded, Hale. The one that matters is the zero coming off, and I'm still waiting on who decided to enter it before anyone called me.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.

I need the zero withdrawn and an apology that Owen heard about this from his phone in the middle of class. If you have something beyond a software score, now is when you say it, because otherwise I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
